messages:
anya: Quick question — we're seeing customer SIEMs complain about holes in audit streams when they use S3 export + sampling. Is this expected?

mike: Do you mean sampling at the producer side (our exporter) or configured on the customer's SIEM?

anya: Producer side. Some customers ask us to sample to reduce cost. They then tell us Splunk/Datadog miss correlated events (start/stop) so investigations are harder.

jordan: Sampling can break causal chains. If we drop events like session.start or auth.success, downstream correlation and alerting suffer. Need to ensure we never sample critical event types.

liz: Customer story: legal asked for immutable audit of RBAC changes. They had sampling enabled, and a privilege escalation investigation hit a blind spot. They want guarantees.

mike: Agreed. Proposal: introduce a two-tier sampler. 1) Always keep events with event_type in a protected set (rbac.*, auth.*, audit.config.*). 2) Sample the rest by rate or fraction.

anya: That sounds good. Also want to know how KMS rotation affects S3 export signatures. We had a rotated key for one tenant and they said some old deliveries couldn't be decrypted in their SIEM ingestion lambda.

security-bot: FYI: KMS rotation should be transparent if envelope encryption is used and we update metadata.kms_key_id on re-encrypt. But if downstream expects a fixed key id in header it can fail.

mike: Right — we rely on envelope encryption + include a kms_key_id header in the exported manifest. If key rotates we add the new id and keep previous ids for decrypting older objects. Customer ingestion code must accept rewrapped ciphertexts.

jordan: Action item: add a line to SDK/webhook docs about accepting new kms_key_id values and fallback to previous versions. Also update onboarding checklist to highlight that SIEM lambda must not hardcode key IDs.

anya: Back to schema: some customers asked for an event.trace_id field to tie multi-object exports together. We currently have event.request_id and object.manifest_id but no global trace. Thoughts?

mike: Adding event.trace_id is fine. It should be stable across retries and across objects produced for the same logical request. Implement in runtime: generate UUIDv4 at request entrance and propagate.

jordan: We'll need to bump schema minor version, document mapping to common SIEM fields (ecs.trace.id for Elastic, traceId for Splunk) and provide migration notes.

liz: Can we include a small sample payload for customers showing S3 object metadata + manifest? That's what they keep asking for.

mike: Sample:

```
{
  "event": {
    "type": "rbac.role.update",
    "timestamp": "2026-03-12T14:21:00Z",
    "request_id": "req_01F...",
    "trace_id": "trace_7a9f..."
  },
  "actor": { "id": "user:123", "role": "admin" },
  "object": { "type": "role", "id": "role-xyz", "manifest_id": "m_0001" },
  "delivery": { "s3_key": "s3://redwood-exports/tenant-42/2026-03-12/m_0001.json.enc", "kms_key_id": "arn:aws:kms:...:key/abc" }
}
```

jordan: Good. Also add a top-level "sampling_reason" when an event was suppressed or partial, e.g., "sampling:low_freq" so customers can know gaps are intentional. But do not add it for protected events (we never sample those).

anya: Nice. For webhooks (real-time) we also need to ensure we surface X-Redwood-Trace and X-Redwood-Signature headers. Customers often parse only the JSON and miss headers.

security-bot: Recommend: put critical metadata both in headers and in the payload metadata block. That way if a proxy strips headers, downstream still sees trace/sign info.

liz: Onboarding change: update the SIEM checklist to include 1) support for trace_id across objects, 2) accept kms key rotations, 3) whitelist our s3 prefixes, 4) do not rely on sampling for audit-critical event types.

mike: For RBAC changes during deployment: if role IDs are renamed we should emit an event mapping old->new. Otherwise lookups fail in customer's enrichment pipelines.

jordan: Yep. Emit rbac.mapping events on rename operations. And ensure we store previous role IDs in the object for a TTL (30 days) to aid backfills.

anya: TL;DR action items:
- mike: implement protected event whitelist + sampling policy docs
- mike: add trace_id generation and propagate to manifest
- jordan: bump audit schema minor, add mapping docs and ECS/SIEM field mappings
- jordan: add rbac.mapping event on rename + 30d previous ids retention
- liz: update onboarding checklist and customer sample payloads
- ops: verify KMS rotation behavior with an S3 decrypt consumer and publish guidance

mike: I'll open a PR for the runtime changes and a docs PR.

jordan: I'll draft the schema change proposal and send for review.

liz: I'll start an onboarding doc draft and ping support channel for customers who reported missing data.

sre-bot: Deploy window reminder: please avoid secret rotation at 23:00 UTC while we test decrypt path.

anya: Thanks all — let's sync if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
